items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: George played all different man with Kid Punch. Last time he left and he played with Kid Punch.

ctx.x: So he played around here, wasn't he? This is home, yeah, sure. He played too.

Who did George play with? Who did George play with? Who did George? Foster. Who George? George played all different man with Kid Punch. Last time he left and he played with Kid Punch. Yeah, with Punch. George left and he went to New York, not New York, Chicago. That's why he made them records with Lewis, you know what I mean? The Kid Oren and Hot Fire. George Foster. He be jeezing all that thing, you know what I mean? He made all that stuff, you know what I mean? Muscat Rambles. George and all that recording.
Did you play with a brass band in different range? No. Did you ever play with any brass bands here in the city?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: No, I don't think nobody in the world them days could beat Punch playing a blues number.

ctx.x: . . . . . . . It was 21, street they called Corner and Roman. It was like you said, two, that time they had wagons. It was Punch with his band and Kid Rene with his band, but he happened to have two corners. Rick, I was playing with him that Sunday. And the first number they played, I was just, I think it was Panama. And then they came back and Punch picked up a good blues number. No, I don't think nobody in the world them days could beat Punch playing a blues number. Couldn't beat that man with a blues number.…
I know where it comes from, but I never know it being orchestrated. But the boys got the number. The boys got the number. The boys got the number. You want to bring out. I know that.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Like Willie Paggio, Kid Rene, all them parts like that, Punch and all of them.

ctx.x: Well, what about Kid Rene? You worked with him some, I think you're talking about. Oh yeah, I worked with Rene.

A whole lot of different jobs, yeah. Well, I worked with putting all the musicians in the city, especially if your musicians come up in my time, you know. Like Willie Paggio, Kid Rene, all them parts like that, Punch and all of them.
Well, what about Rene? What band did he in? Where did he work? Well, Rene worked all different places, you know.
